questions.question: Adding antioxidants to oily food slows down rancidity.
A reaction that releases heat is called ____.
A reaction that absorbs heat is called ____.
Coating iron with zinc to prevent rusting is called ____.
Distinguish exothermic and endothermic reactions, with one example each.
questions.answer: Exothermic: releases heat to surroundings; the surroundings warm up. Example: 2 Mg + O₂ → 2 MgO (with heat and light). Endothermic: absorbs heat from surroundings; the surroundings cool down. Example: photosynthesis (6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂; absorbs sunlight).

questions.question: Balance these step-by-step: (i) Pb + AgNO₃ → Pb(NO₃)₂ + Ag, (ii) C₃H₈ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O.
questions.answer: (i) Pb + 2 AgNO₃ → Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2 Ag. (1 Pb, 2 Ag, 2 NO₃ each side ✓.) (ii) C₃H₈ + 5 O₂ → 3 CO₂ + 4 H₂O. (3 C, 8 H, 10 O each side ✓.)

questions.question: What is rancidity? Suggest THREE methods to prevent it.
questions.answer: RANCIDITY is the development of an unpleasant smell and taste in oily / fatty foods due to slow oxidation of the fats. Three prevention methods: (1) airtight packaging (often flushed with nitrogen); (2) addition of antioxidants (BHA, BHT); (3) refrigeration to slow the oxidation reaction. (Also valid: vacuum packing, dark / opaque bottles.)

questions.question: Balance the following four equations and classify each by reaction type. (a) Na + H₂O → NaOH + H₂. (b) ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂. (c) AgNO₃ + KCl → AgCl + KNO₃. (d) C + O₂ → CO₂.
questions.answer: (a) 2 Na + 2 H₂O → 2 NaOH + H₂. Type: DISPLACEMENT (Na displaces H from water). (b) ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂. Type: DECOMPOSITION (already balanced). (c) AgNO₃ + KCl → AgCl + KNO₃. Type: DOUBLE DISPLACEMENT (already balanced). (d) C + O₂ → CO₂. Type: COMBINATION (already balanced).

questions.question: A school is planning to install new iron benches outdoors near the seaside. The headmaster is worried about rusting. As a chemistry student, give a structured plan with at least THREE prevention strategies, and explain WHY each works.
questions.answer: Three prevention strategies, each with reasoning: (1) PAINT all iron surfaces with rust-resistant primer + topcoat. WHY: paint is a physical barrier that keeps oxygen and moisture away from the iron. (2) Use GALVANISED iron (zinc-coated iron) for the benches OR coat existing iron with zinc. WHY: zinc is more reactive than iron, so zinc oxidises preferentially (sacrificial protection) — even if the surface is scratched, the zinc still protects the iron. (3) Apply ANTI-RUST OIL or grease at all joints / hinges; re-apply every few months. WHY: oil prevents oxygen and water from reaching the iron. (Bonus strategy 4) Use STAINLESS STEEL where possible — its chromium content forms an invisible passive oxide layer that prevents further corrosion. (Bonus 5) Keep the benches CLEAN of salt deposits — salt accelerates corrosion.
questions.explanation: Practical, multi-strategy answer to a real problem.
